title: One-Hour Broiled Chicken Prep: Trimming, Spatchcocking, and Carving with Lan Lam (ATK Techniquely)
summary: In this ATK Techniquely episode, Lan Lam demonstrates comprehensive prep techniques for whole chicken and its parts to streamline pan-searing/broiling and to improve cook evenness and presentation. The video covers cavity inspection and trimming, choosing between scissors and knife for trimming, backbone removal and spatchcocking, wing-tucking and leg-tying with twine, oiling and seasoning inside and out, and a skillet-first broil finish. It then walks through splitting and trimming bone-in and boneless breasts, trimming and deboning thighs, and preparing drumsticks, followed by resting, carving, and finishing with a simple pan sauce from the roasted juices. The lesson emphasizes practical knife work, fat management, and portioning cuts for even cooking, with tips on tool choice and rest-time gains in texture and flavor.

sections.title: Whole chicken prep: cavity inspection and trimming
sections.description: Lan starts with whole-chicken prep, inspecting the cavity for spare parts, then trims excess skin and fat with scissors or knife, noting trimmings can flavor gravy. He emphasizes that birds vary in wing position and that trimming is the step many recipes assume you know.

sections.title: Backbone removal and spatchcock prep
concepts: snipping along the backbone with kitchen shears
working on one side then the other
sections.description: The video demonstrates removing the backbone to flatten the bird for faster, more even cooking, using careful, short snips along the bone to avoid hip-bone obstruction, and notes freezing backbone scraps for later stock.

sections.title: Seasoning: oil, salt, pepper, and leg-tie prep
concepts: seasoning inside and outside with salt and pepper
sections.description: After backbone removal, Lan seasons the bird (oil, salt, pepper) and discusses whether to tuck wings, then covers leg-tying prep and the rationale behind a taut knot to secure the bird for roasting.

sections.title: Skillet roasting method and broiler finish
concepts: preheating a skillet with oil until it smokes
sections.description: Lan explains a fast, skillet-centric approach: heat the skillet with a small oil amount until smoking, place the bird in a cold-oven setup, and finish under the broiler for quick browning and a faster route to a cooked bird.

sections.title: Split breasts prep: trimming and portioning
concepts: anatomy of split breasts: rib cage vs keel bone
removing side fat and rib bits
sections.description: Two methods for prep are shown: using kitchen shears or a knife to trim excess skin and fat around split breasts, with attention to the keel bone, rib cage, and ensuring clean, neat portions for even cooking.

sections.title: Dark meat prep: thighs and bones, skin decisions
concepts: trimming excess junk from bone-in thighs
removing surface fat and trimming pockets
bone removal while preserving skin when desired
sections.description: This section covers trimming and deboning thighs (bone-in and skin-on, plus skinless variants), fat pocket removal, and strategies for preserving skin when deboning, highlighting how bone structure and skin affect cooking and flavor.

sections.title: Drumstick prep and thigh balancing tips
concepts: keeping equipment sharp for clean incisions
sections.description: Drumsticks are trimmed and slashed to reduce cooking time and promote tenderness, with emphasis on keeping the skin taut to avoid slipping and maximizing control during cuts.

sections.title: Tools, resting, carving, and pan sauce
concepts: knife choice: small chef's knives vs larger blades
pan sauce from roasted juices with garlic and thyme
sections.description: Lan discusses tool selection (petty/boning knives for easier maneuvering), resting time to finish flavor development, carving strategy to maximize yield and minimize waste, and finishing with a quick pan sauce from the roasting juices infused with garlic and thyme.
